newsitem.title: USA: US House panel rejects plan to raise cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: US House panel rejects plan to raise cigarette tax.

text.p: The U.S. House tax writing committee on Thursday rejected a proposal that would have raised taxes on cigarettes by 29 cents per pack to 53 cents.

The amendment was offered by Rep. Nancy Johnson, a Connecticut Republican, who had sought to inject the proposal into the larger tax bill that the House Ways and Means Committee is currently considering.
Johnson met resistance from other Republicans on the committee, especially those from tobacco-producing states.
"It serves no purpose at all. It just adds more revenue to a bill that's already paid for," said Rep. Jim Bunning, a Kentucky Republican said.
Revenues raised from the proposed tax increase would have amounted to $30.2 billion over five years.
The current federal tax on cigarettes is 24 cents per pack.
